speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: Who triumphs, and what is he the treasury of?
premises: He who, made of the widely flashing wheel of diverse states, comes to be the objects of experience.
Whose one is given to contemplation, thus the bond of nondifference: Śaṃbhura, woe-averting, triumphs — treasury of the lights of knowing.
inference: The mangala invokes the knowing-treasury: the bhāva-cakra's nondifference-bond names what the work stores — bodha-bhāsās.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: Why is the Gītā held supreme among expositions?
premises: By the sage Dvaipāyana this scripture was expounded, measured by hundreds of thousands; here liberation is established as the fruit.
Other dharma-and-rest of it is recited to nourish that fruit [mādhānyataḥ: LIVE fork, grounds in L0].

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: What is liberation named as?
premises: Liberation by name is complete-differentiation in form, all-knowing, auspicious-natured, free from need, in Bhagavān the Lord, ever-risen.
Dissolution — this much [prathiḥ: LIVE fork] — in summary.
inference: Mokṣa is defined by compound-nature (saṃskāra-svabhāva, sarvajña, nityodita) and reduced to laya in samāsa — the forked 'this-much-toward-it' held open.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: How does the Gītā compare to other mokṣa-celebrations?
premises: Although liberation by name is celebrated in other connections, yet the Bhagavadgītā is the giver of true attainment.
inference: Other texts sing mokṣa incidentally; the Gītā gives samyak-prāpti — the supremacy claim is exclusive (samyak retained).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: Why write another exposition?
premises: Earlier ones made many expositions among them, yet this attempt is reasonable — revealing its hidden meaning.
inference: The udyama is justified by gūḍhārtha-prakāśana: prior vyākhyās are many, this one discloses the hidden sense (bhāṣya not prakaraṇa).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: What is this work's colophon?
premises: From Bhaṭṭa Indurāja's oral tradition, examined long with thought, made by Abhinavagupta — this here is the Gītārthasaṃgraha.
inference: The verse seals authorship: āmnāya from Bhaṭṭa Indurāja (his Pratyabhijñā teacher), long vivicana, kṛta by Abhinavagupta — the name declared.
